requirements.verifier_assertion: Starting llama-server without -m/-hf/... enters router mode: the main process loads no model itself. tests/test_outputs.py:170-198 starts the router with no model flags and asserts the process stays up serving /v1/models.
--models-dir PATH is the mechanism the router uses to discover servable models. tests/test_outputs.py:171 passes --models-dir MODELS_DIR at startup; the router must accept and honour it.
Top-level GGUF files are named by stripping the .gguf suffix. tests/test_outputs.py:222-228 asserts models list contains ids {tiny-a, tiny-b} for /opt/models/tiny-a.gguf and /opt/models/tiny-b.gguf.

A GGUF placed inside a subdirectory of --models-dir makes the entire subdirectory count as one model named after the directory. tests/test_outputs.py:222-228 asserts id tiny-c (subdirectory) with path ending in tiny-c/tiny-c.gguf.
must_include: entire subdirectory counts as one model

requirements.verifier_assertion: --models-max N controls the maximum simultaneously-loaded models; default 4 and 0 means unlimited. tests/test_outputs.py:389-401 starts the router with --models-max 1 to exercise the limit.

Exceeding --models-max causes automatic unload of the least recently used loaded model. tests/test_outputs.py:389-401 loads MODEL_A, touches it, then loads MODEL_C and asserts MODEL_A transitions to unloaded while MODEL_C is loaded.

--models-allow-extra-args is off by default; when off the extra_args field on the load endpoint must be ignored. tests/test_outputs.py exercises the flag semantics indirectly by requiring the default startup args reported on load to be a non-empty array (line 254).

Inference-related parameters given to the router at startup (for example -ctx, -n) must be passed through as defaults to every spawned instance. Reflected in tests/test_outputs.py:253-254 which asserts loaded status carries a non-empty args array.
must_include: passed through as defaults to every model instance

requirements.verifier_assertion: GET /models and GET /v1/models return the OpenAI-compatible {"object": "list", "data": [...]} envelope. tests/test_outputs.py:75-76 asserts status==200 and body.object=='list'; :232-235 asserts alias /models returns same ids.

Each model entry carries id, in_cache (false for --models-dir entries), path, and status. tests/test_outputs.py:222-229 asserts these fields, including in_cache is False and path ends with the expected relative filename.
must_include: in_cache (boolean, false for models coming from --models-dir)

requirements.verifier_assertion: The status object's value is one of unloaded/loading/loaded; loaded status carries a non-empty args array; a failed load returns to unloaded with failed:true and exit_code. tests/test_outputs.py:84-99 polls status; :229 asserts initial value=='unloaded'; :253-254 asserts loaded carries non-empty args.
must_include: the array of startup arguments actually used by that model instance

requirements.verifier_assertion: POST /models/load with {"model": name} returns 200 + {success:true} on success (tests/test_outputs.py:104-106), 404 with error.type=="not_found_error" for an unknown model (:263-265), and 400 for an already-loaded model (:273-275).
POST /models/unload with {"model": name} returns 200 + {success:true} on success (tests/test_outputs.py:111-113); 400 for unknown model (:285-287); 400 for a not-loaded model (:280-282).
must_include: Model is not currently in the loaded state → 400

requirements.verifier_assertion: POST inference endpoints route by the "model" field in the JSON body. tests/test_outputs.py:296-305 posts /v1/completions with model==MODEL_A and asserts 200 + non-empty choices[0].text; :311-323 posts /v1/chat/completions with model==MODEL_B and asserts assistant message. :329-337 asserts missing/unknown model → 400.
must_include: "model" field in the JSON request body
A model name that does not exist → 400

requirements.verifier_assertion: GET endpoints like /props route by URL query ?model=... (URL-encoded). tests/test_outputs.py:340-347 GETs /props?model=<urlquoted> and asserts a routed response.

Autoload is on by default. tests/test_outputs.py:294-308 POSTs /v1/completions against an unloaded model without any autoload override and asserts 200 + choices; :308 asserts the model ended up loaded.
--no-models-autoload at startup disables autoload globally. tests/test_outputs.py:355 starts the router with [--no-models-autoload]; :356-360 asserts /v1/completions on an unloaded model returns 400.

?autoload=false disables autoload for one request. tests/test_outputs.py:372-377 POSTs /v1/completions?autoload=false against an unloaded model and asserts 400 + the model stays unloaded; :380-382 asserts a follow-up without the flag returns 200.
When autoload is disabled, a request for an unloaded model returns 400. tests/test_outputs.py:359 and :375 both assert status==400 in this configuration.
GET /props without a model parameter returns the router's own info with role=="router". tests/test_outputs.py:239-242 asserts status==200 and body.role=='router'.
must_include: role field must be set to "router"

requirements.verifier_assertion: Each spawned model instance exposes its own /props with model_alias equal to the model name. tests/test_outputs.py:340-347 asserts a /props routed to MODEL_A carries model_alias == MODEL_A.
must_include: model_alias field in its /props equals the corresponding model name

requirements.verifier_assertion: Routing is transparent to callers — the response is the instance's own response with the usual choices/message shape. tests/test_outputs.py:300-305 (choices+text+finish_reason=='length') and :318-323 (message.role=='assistant', non-empty content) rely on transparent pass-through.

Three tiny GGUFs at /opt/models/tiny-a.gguf, /opt/models/tiny-b.gguf, /opt/models/tiny-c/tiny-c.gguf; ids tiny-a, tiny-b, tiny-c. tests/test_outputs.py:33-36 pins the ids; :222-228 pins the relative paths.

The verifier builds llama-server incrementally and exercises the whole list→load→routing→unload→eviction flow. tests/test_outputs.py:120-142 configures + builds via cmake and asserts the binary; every subsequent test hits the running router with curl-equivalent HTTP.
must_include: list, load, inference routing including autoload, unload, and eviction

requirements.verifier_assertion: During verify the agent must not use pkill -f llama-server because the harness runs the agent CLI with the task text (which contains the substring llama-server) in its command line. tests/test_outputs.py:210-212 uses `pkill -x llama-server` (exact match) in teardown, which is the recommended pattern.
